name: Gideoni
title: Father of Abidan, leader from Benjamin
summary: Gideoni was the father of Abidan, who served as a leader and chieftain of the tribe of Benjamin during the wilderness journey. He is mentioned in connection with the census and the tribal offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle. Although little is known about him personally, his family held significance in Israel's early history.

keyEvents.title: Abidan appointed as leader of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: Abidan, son of Gideoni, was chosen to lead the tribe of Benjamin and assist Moses with the census.

keyEvents.title: Abidan among the tribal princes
keyEvents.description: Abidan, son of Gideoni, stood as head of the army of the tribe of Benjamin during the mustering of Israel's people.

keyEvents.title: Counting of the tribe of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: The tribe of Benjamin was counted under the leadership of Abidan, son of Gideoni, and numbered 35,400 men fit for battle.

keyEvents.title: Abidan's offering at the altar
keyEvents.description: Abidan, son of Gideoni, presented his offering on the ninth day during the dedication of the tabernacle's altar.

keyEvents.title: Abidan leads the camp of Benjamin during the march
keyEvents.description: During Israel's march through the wilderness, Abidan son of Gideoni led the division from the tribe of Benjamin.
